prompt:
You watch a short video made ONLY of these clips, played back to back with NO narration between them.
Each clip is a person's own words from a show; the shows were not in one conversation. The first clip (label "hook")
opens the video. The hook is shown for context only: it is NOT rated here (its own job was judged on its own).

CLIP label="hook" (on screen: Simply Bitcoin): "Bitcoin is money that lives on nodes, thousands of computers running all across the world, thousands of computers that have a ledger, a blockchain, a time chain of the truth, of all of the transactions that have ever happened on the network, who owns what, how much do people own?"
CLIP label="clip_01" (on screen: Simply Bitcoin): "One, yes, institutions are here. Wall Street is interested in Bitcoin, you know, J.P. Morgan, BlackRock, et cetera, et cetera. But there's still a lot of pushback from these institutions. They really don't want to let Bitcoin through the gate."
CLIP label="clip_02" (on screen: Scott Melker): "We joked that we knew Bitcoin was going to make it when there wouldn't be just fun culture of Bitcoin conferences anymore. And the conferences that we first met, like those were so fun. But we used to have having parties. And people still do them."

1) Played back to back with no narration, is there a through-line a viewer can state? State it in ONE sentence, or
   "none" if there is none.
2) For each clip AFTER the hook, rate 1-5 how much it advances that through-line (5 = essential, 1 = off topic).
3) For each JOIN between two consecutive clips, the hook's own join included (does the hook set up the clip after
   it?): could a viewer follow the jump with no narration, i.e. is the next clip's subject or referent clear coming
   from the previous clip's ending? Answer true or false, and why in a few words.
Return ONLY this JSON object: {"through_line": "...", "clips": {"clip_01": 1, "clip_02": 1}, "joins": {"hook -> clip_01": {"followable": true, "why": "..."}, "clip_01 -> clip_02": {"followable": true, "why": "..."}}}
text: {"through_line": "Bitcoin's growing institutional interest and cultural shift toward mainstream acceptance despite resistance.", "clips": {"clip_01": 4, "clip_02": 3}, "joins": {"hook -> clip_01": {"followable": false, "why": "Hook ends on blockchain ownership; clip_01 starts numbered point on institutions with no clear link"}, "clip_01 -> clip_02": {"followable": false, "why": "Shifts from institutional pushback to evolving Bitcoin conference culture without direct referent"}}}
